attempts.decision_title: Synthetic cannabinoid fine outside tracker scope
attempts.explanation: The article reports that the Czech State Agricultural and Food Inspection (SZPI) fined a tobacconist in Sokolov 100,000 crowns at the end of October 2026 for selling blue Vapoverde packets sold under the name Legal Cannabis 420: dried hemp sprayed with the synthetic cannabinoids MDMB-PINACA and MDMB-INACA, which are on the Czech list of prohibited psychoactive substances. The police investigation described in the piece concerns only the sale of that synthetic product to a minor girl who collapsed and was hospitalised, handled as an offence (přestupek) referred to the Sokolov municipal authority, while the distributor Vapoverde was left unsanctioned. Under the tracker's substance scope, synthetic cannabinoids and their precursors are out of scope, including hemp used only as their carrier, so this is not relevant rather than routed to the CFI history; the sources describe no separate natural cannabis enforcement component. No existing report covers this case, so no merge or update applies.

report.title: Police destroy 53,000 cannabis plants on two farms at Yaruni Bend, Linden
report.summary: Guyanese police destroyed approximately 53,000 suspected cannabis plants, two makeshift camps, two drying areas and 10 pounds of dried cannabis on two farms covering about eight acres at Yaruni Bend, Linden, in the Upper Demerara River area. Police estimated the value of the narcotics destroyed at $22,038,728 and made no arrests, with investigations continuing.
report.place: Yaruni Bend, Linden, Upper Demerara River

sources.title: Police destroy 53,000 cannabis plants in Linden eradication exercise

open_questions: The plant count, the eight-acre area and the $22,038,728 valuation are police estimates published by a single outlet, with no independent measurement.
Only one accessible account of this operation was found after searching in English, so the whole report rests on that single source.
The plants and the dried material are described as suspected cannabis, with no laboratory confirmation reported.
No suspects or farm owners were named, and no later investigation outcome was reported.
Yaruni Bend is not mapped in the source, so the coordinates mark Linden, the named town, rather than the farm site itself.
report.body:
Police destroyed approximately 53,000 suspected cannabis plants after finding
two farms covering about eight acres, about 3.24 hectares, at Yaruni Bend,
Linden, in the Upper Demerara River area. The eradication exercise was
conducted by police ranks led by a Gazetted Officer between 5:30 a.m. and 4:36
p.m. on Thursday, 10 September 2026. The plants, which ranged between two
and six feet in height, were found on two separate cannabis farms.

Ranks also discovered two makeshift camps and two drying areas containing a
combined 10 pounds, about 4.54 kilograms, of dried cannabis. The suspected
cannabis plants, the dried cannabis, the camps and the drying areas were
destroyed by fire. Police estimated the total value of the narcotics
destroyed at $22,038,728.

No arrests were made, and investigations are continuing.

attempts.explanation: The source reports that 46-year-old musician Mak Faden Jesse Sorato, who performs as JESSE, was arrested by Tokyo police on suspicion of violating Japan's Cannabis Control Law by using cocaine; officers from the Shibuya Police Station drug investigation unit searched his home and a urine test was positive, and he reportedly admitted most of the suspicion. The tracker covers enforcement involving cannabis plants and cannabis products such as marijuana, hashish, resin, oil and edibles. Cocaine is not cannabis, and no cannabis seizure, possession or use forms part of this arrest, so the event has no cannabis component and is outside the tracker's substance scope. This is an out-of-scope enforcement event, not a law change or precedent, so it is not routed to the Cannabis Freedom Index. His 2019 conviction for cannabis and cocaine possession is a separate prior case and does not bring this arrest into scope. No existing tracker report on this JESSE arrest was found, and the nominated Zambia report concerns a different event.

attempts.decision_title: Missouri intoxicating hemp law takes effect; routed to CFI
attempts.explanation: The submitted Spectrum News St. Louis article reports that Missouri's Intoxicating Cannabinoid Control Act took effect on 12 November 2026, reclassifying hemp-derived products containing more than 0.4 milligrams of THC as marijuana and restricting their cultivation and sale to businesses licensed under the state marijuana program. That is a change in the law, not an enforcement event: this tracker records raids, seizures, arrests, prosecutions and sentences, while law changes and rulings that set a precedent belong to the Cannabis Freedom Index history, so this is routed there rather than drafted as a tracker report. The article only mentions in passing, without names, dates, places or figures, that the Attorney General's office has sued four businesses said to be selling such products and that a federal court dismissed the Missouri Hemp Trade Association's constitutional challenge; neither can support a single sourced enforcement report here.
